issuing_body: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
title: Minn. Stat. § 388.051 — Duties of County Attorney
supports: County attorneys have a general statutory duty to prosecute felonies in their counties, including drawing indictments found by a grand jury.
County attorneys also prosecute gross misdemeanors, misdemeanors, petty misdemeanors and other offenses to the extent prescribed by law.

This is the general Minnesota allocation of local felony prosecution authority and must be read alongside statutes granting the Attorney General direct authority in specific subject areas such as Medicaid.
selected_locators: Subd. 1(3) — prosecute felonies and other offenses
important_qualifications: This general county-attorney duty does not negate subject-specific statutes authorizing the Attorney General to prosecute or bring civil actions.
The statute does not establish which prosecutor handled or should have handled any particular fraud matter; that requires the case-specific referral and charging record.
